formulations.label: Hard capsules
formulations.note: Capsules are for adults only; the paediatric starting dose uses the oral liquid. Capsule and oral solution are bioequivalent.

src.q: Each capsule contains fluoxetine hydrochloride equivalent to 20mg fluoxetine.
Fluoxetine capsules are meant for oral administration in adults only.
The capsule and oral solution forms are bioequivalent.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Adults: major depressive episodes; obsessive-compulsive disorder; bulimia nervosa (with psychotherapy). Children and adolescents 8 years and over: moderate to severe major depressive episode not responding to 4 to 6 sessions of psychological therapy (given with psychological therapy).

src.q: Adults: Major depressive disorders/episodes. Obsessive-compulsive disorder. Bulimia nervosa
Moderate to severe major depressive episode, if depression is unresponsive to psychological therapy after 4-6 sessions.

items.t: Children 8 to 18 years: depression only, started and monitored under specialist supervision, with concurrent psychological therapy.

src.q: Treatment should be initiated and monitored under specialist supervision.
should only be used in children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years for the treatment of moderate to severe major depressive episodes and it should not be used in other indications

items.t: 20 mg daily; review within 3 to 4 weeks. If response is insufficient, increase gradually up to 60 mg daily. Treat at least 6 months.

src.q: A dose of 20 mg/day is recommended. Dosage should be reviewed and adjusted if necessary, within 3 to 4 weeks of initiation of therapy
the dose may be increased gradually up to a maximum of 60mg
Patients with depression should be treated for a sufficient period of at least 6 months to ensure that they are free from symptoms.

items.t: 20 mg daily; if response is insufficient after 2 weeks, increase gradually up to 60 mg. Reconsider if no improvement within 10 weeks.

src.q: Obsessive-compulsive disorder Adults and the elderly: The recommended dose is 20mg daily.
If no improvement is observed within 10 weeks, treatment with fluoxetine should be reconsidered.

items.t: 60 mg daily.

src.q: Bulimia nervosa Adults and the elderly: A dose of 60 mg/day is recommended.

items.t: Elderly: caution when increasing; usually not more than 40 mg daily (maximum 60 mg daily).

src.q: Caution is recommended when increasing the dose, and the daily dose should generally not exceed 40mg. Maximum recommended dose is 60mg/day.

items.t: Hepatic impairment or interacting medicines: consider a lower or less frequent dose (e.g. 20 mg every second day).

src.q: A lower or less frequent dose (eg, 20mg every second day) should be considered in patients with hepatic impairment

items.t: Stopping: avoid abrupt withdrawal; reduce gradually over at least 1 to 2 weeks. The drug persists in the body for weeks after stopping.

src.q: When stopping treatment with FLUOXETINE the dose should be gradually reduced over a period of at least one to two weeks in order to reduce the risk of withdrawal reactions
When dosing is stopped, active drug substances will persist in the body for weeks.

items.t: 8 years and over (moderate to severe depression): start 10 mg/day as 2.5 ml of the liquid; after 1 to 2 weeks may increase to 20 mg/day. Lower-weight children may need lower doses. Review need after 6 months; reconsider if no benefit within 9 weeks.

src.q: The starting dose is 10mg/day given as 2.5ml of the FLUOXETINE liquid formulation.
After one to two weeks, the dose may be increased to 20mg/day.
If no clinical benefit is achieved within 9 weeks, treatment should be reconsidered.

items.t: Monitor growth and puberty (height, weight, Tanner stage) during and after treatment; monitor for mania/hypomania and suicidal symptoms.

src.q: Growth and pubertal development (height, weight, and TANNER staging) should therefore be monitored during and after treatment with fluoxetine.
regular monitoring for the occurrence of mania/hypomania is recommended

items.t: Hypersensitivity to fluoxetine or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Irreversible non-selective MAOIs (e.g. iproniazid): start fluoxetine 2 weeks after stopping one; wait at least 5 weeks after fluoxetine before starting one.

src.q: Fluoxetine is contra-indicated in combination with irreversible, non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitors (e.g. iproniazid)
at least 5 weeks should elapse after discontinuing fluoxetine treatment before starting an irreversible, non-selective MAOI

items.t: Metoprolol used in heart failure (excess bradycardia).

src.q: Fluoxetine is contra-indicated in combination with metoprolol used in cardiac failure

items.t: Seizures: introduce cautiously if history of seizures; avoid in unstable epilepsy; monitor controlled epilepsy carefully; stop if seizures develop or increase.

src.q: fluoxetine should be introduced cautiously in patients who have a history of seizures
Fluoxetine should be avoided in patients with unstable seizure disorders/epilepsy and patients with controlled epilepsy should be carefully monitored

items.t: QT prolongation and torsade de pointes reported: use with caution in congenital long QT, family history, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia, acute MI, uncompensated heart failure, hepatic impairment or with QT-prolonging drugs. Stable cardiac disease: consider ECG review before starting.

src.q: Fluoxetine should be used with caution in patients with conditions such as congenital long QT syndrome, a family history of QT prolongation or other clinical conditions that predispose to arrhythmias
If patients with stable cardiac disease are treated, an ECG review should be considered before treatment is started.

items.t: Bleeding: caution with oral anticoagulants, antiplatelets (aspirin), NSAIDs and in bleeding disorders. SSRIs may increase postpartum haemorrhage.

src.q: Caution is advised in patients taking SSRIs, particularly in concomitant use with oral anticoagulants, drugs known to affect platelet function
SSRIs/SNRIs may increase the risk of postpartum haemorrhage

items.t: Rash or allergic reactions with no other cause: stop fluoxetine (serious systemic reactions reported).

src.q: Upon the appearance of rash or of other allergic phenomena for which an alternative aetiology cannot be identified, fluoxetine should be discontinued.

items.t: Suicidal thoughts/behaviour: close supervision early and after dose changes, especially under 25 years.

src.q: Close supervision of patients and in particular those at high risk should accompany drug therapy especially in early treatment and following dose changes.

items.t: Mania history: use with caution; stop if manic. Diabetes: hypoglycaemia on treatment, hyperglycaemia after stopping; adjust antidiabetic doses.

src.q: Antidepressants should be used with caution in patients with a history of mania/hypomania.
Hypoglycaemia has been reported during therapy with fluoxetine and hyperglycaemia has developed following discontinuation.

items.t: Serotonin syndrome or NMS-like events (with other serotonergic or neuroleptic drugs): stop fluoxetine and give supportive care.

src.q: treatment with fluoxetine should be discontinued if such events

items.t: Raised intraocular pressure or risk of narrow-angle glaucoma: caution (mydriasis). Acute cardiac disease: caution.

src.q: caution should be used when prescribing fluoxetine in patients with raised intraocular pressure or those at risk of acute narrow-angle glaucoma
Clinical experience in acute cardiac disease is limited, therefore caution is advisable.

items.t: Akathisia in first weeks; withdrawal symptoms (common); ECT may prolong seizures; sexual dysfunction that may persist after stopping; weight loss.

src.q: There have been rare reports of prolonged seizures in patients on fluoxetine receiving ECT treatment; therefore, caution is advisable.
There have been reports of long-lasting sexual dysfunction where the symptoms have continued despite discontinuation of SSRIs/SNRI.

items.t: Long half-lives of fluoxetine and norfluoxetine: interactions may occur for weeks after stopping (e.g. when switching antidepressants).

src.q: The long elimination half-lives of both fluoxetine and norfluoxetine should be borne in mind

items.t: Contraindicated: irreversible non-selective MAOIs; metoprolol in heart failure. Not recommended: tamoxifen (avoid whenever possible), alcohol, linezolid or methylene blue (if unavoidable, close monitoring and low starting doses), mequitazine.

src.q: co-administration with potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (including fluoxetine) should whenever possible be avoided
close clinical monitoring should be undertaken and the concomitant agents should be initiated at the lower recommended doses

items.t: Serotonergic drugs (lithium, tramadol, triptans, tryptophan, selegiline, St John's wort): caution with closer, more frequent monitoring. The St John's wort herbal SPC says do not take it with SSRIs.

src.q: the concomitant use of fluoxetine with these drugs should be undertaken with caution, with closer and more frequent clinical monitoring
SSRIs e.g. Citalopram Escitalopram Fluoxetine Fluvoxamine Paroxetine Sertraline

items.t: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, TCAs, some antimicrobials such as moxifloxacin): use with caution.

src.q: anti-malaria treatment particularly halofantrine, certain antihistamines (astemizole, mizolastine), should be used with caution

items.t: Oral anticoagulants, antiplatelets including aspirin, NSAIDs: increased bleeding; clinical monitoring and more frequent INR checks with oral anticoagulants.

src.q: Clinical monitoring, and more frequent monitoring of INR with oral anticoagulants, should be made.

items.t: CYP2D6 substrates with narrow therapeutic index or titrated (flecainide, propafenone, nebivolol, atomoxetine, carbamazepine, TCAs, risperidone): start at or adjust to the low end of the dose range (also if fluoxetine taken in the last 5 weeks).

src.q: They should be initiated at or adjusted to the low end of their dose range. This may also apply if fluoxetine has been taken in the previous 5 weeks.

items.t: Phenytoin: level changes, sometimes toxicity; titrate conservatively and monitor. Drugs causing hyponatraemia (diuretics, desmopressin, carbamazepine) and drugs lowering the seizure threshold (TCAs, other SSRIs, tramadol, bupropion) increase risk.

src.q: Use in combination with other agents associated with hyponatremia (e.g. diuretics, desmopressin, carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine) may lead to an increased risk

Use in combination with other agents which may lower the seizure threshold (for example, TCAs, other SSRIs, phenothiazines, butyrophenones, mefloquine, chloroquine, bupropion, tramadol) may lead to an increased risk.

items.t: Severe renal failure on dialysis (GFR <10 ml/min): no difference in plasma levels at 20 mg/day for 2 months. Steady-state levels may rise with repeated dosing.

src.q: patients with severe renal failure (GFR <10ml/min) requiring dialysis showed no difference in plasma levels of fluoxetine or norfluoxetine compared to controls with normal renal function
However, after repeated administration, an increase in steady-state plateau of plasma concentrations may be observed.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: consider a lower or less frequent dose (e.g. 20 mg every second day). Half-lives longer in cirrhosis (7 and 12 days).

src.q: A lower dose, e.g., alternate day dosing, is recommended in patients with significant hepatic dysfunction
fluoxetine and norfluoxetine half-lives are increased to 7 and 12 days, respectively

items.t: SmPC: should not be used unless the woman's condition requires it and justifies the risk to the fetus. Avoid abrupt stopping in pregnancy.

src.q: Fluoxetine should not be used during pregnancy unless the clinical condition of the woman requires treatment with fluoxetine and justifies the potential risk to the foetus.
Abrupt discontinuation of therapy should be avoided during pregnancy

items.t: First trimester: possible small increased risk of cardiovascular defects (about 2/100 vs 1/100). MHRA: weigh this against the benefits of treating depression.

src.q: the risk of having an infant with a cardiovascular defect following maternal fluoxetine exposure is in the region of 2/100 compared with an expected rate for such defects of approximately 1/100
The potential increased risk should be considered in the context of the benefits of treating depression in pregnancy.

items.t: Late pregnancy: caution; neonatal irritability, tremor, hypotonia, crying, sucking or sleeping problems; PPHN about 5 per 1000; postpartum haemorrhage risk under 2-fold after use in the month before birth.

src.q: caution should be exercised, especially during late pregnancy or just prior to the onset of labour
The observed risk was approximately 5 cases per 1000 pregnancies.
Observational data indicate an increased risk (less than 2-fold) of postpartum haemorrhage following SSRI/SNRI exposure within the month prior to birth

items.t: BUMPS: SSRIs are commonly taken in pregnancy without problems; most babies have normal hearts; if well controlled it may be best to stay on fluoxetine. Do not stop without advice. Hospital delivery usually advised.

src.q: SSRIs are commonly taken during pregnancy without any problem.
If a woman's condition is well-controlled with fluoxetine, it may be best to stay on it rather than try something new and risk a relapse.
Women taking an SSRI in pregnancy will usually be advised to have a hospital delivery.

items.t: SmPC: fluoxetine and norfluoxetine pass into milk; infant adverse events reported. If treatment is needed, consider stopping breastfeeding; if breastfeeding continues, use the lowest effective dose.

src.q: Adverse events have been reported in breast-feeding infants.

If treatment with fluoxetine is considered necessary, discontinuation of breast-feeding should be considered; however, if breast-feeding is continued, the lowest effective dose of fluoxetine should be prescribed.

items.t: SPS: can be used with caution (long experience), but sertraline or paroxetine are preferred. Monitor the infant for irritability, restlessness, drowsiness, colic, GI upset, poor feeding and weight gain.

src.q: Fluoxetine can be used with caution. It has been used during breastfeeding for many years, but sertraline or paroxetine are preferred.
As a precaution, monitor for irritability, restlessness, drowsiness, colic, gastro-intestinal disturbances, poor feeding, and adequate weight-gain.

items.t: Animal data: may affect sperm quality; human SSRI reports show it is reversible. Sexual dysfunction may continue after stopping (MHRA 2026 lists fluoxetine).

src.q: Human case reports with some SSRIs have shown that an effect on sperm quality is reversible.
Citalopram, escitalopram, duloxetine, fluvoxamine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline

items.t: Most common: headache, nausea, insomnia, fatigue, diarrhoea; often lessen with continued treatment.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse reactions in patients treated with fluoxetine were headache, nausea, insomnia, fatigue and diarrhoea.
Undesirable effects may decrease in intensity and frequency with continued treatment and do not generally lead to cessation of therapy.

items.t: Withdrawal symptoms on stopping are common (dizziness, sensory disturbance, sleep problems, agitation, nausea, tremor, headache).

src.q: Discontinuation of fluoxetine commonly leads to withdrawal symptoms.

items.t: Serotonin syndrome or NMS-like events (hyperthermia, rigidity, myoclonus, confusion): potentially life-threatening; stop and treat.

src.q: As these syndromes may result in potentially life-threatening conditions, treatment with fluoxetine should be discontinued

items.t: Rash or allergic reaction (including anaphylactoid and serious systemic events): stop if no other cause.

src.q: Rash, anaphylactoid events and progressive systemic events, sometimes serious (involving skin, kidney, liver or lung) have been reported.

items.t: Signs of cardiac arrhythmia: stop and perform an ECG.

src.q: If signs of cardiac arrhythmia occur during treatment with fluoxetine, the treatment should be withdrawn and an ECG should be performed.

items.t: New or worse suicidal thoughts: seek urgent medical attention (MHRA 2026). Abnormal bleeding including GI bleeding.

src.q: if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, particularly when starting or changing dose of antidepressants, seek urgent medical attention
gynaecological haemorrhages, gastro-intestinal bleedings and other cutaneous or mucous bleedings

items.t: Stable cardiac disease: consider ECG review before starting. When starting or changing dose: discuss suicide risk and sexual dysfunction (MHRA 2026).

src.q: If patients with stable cardiac disease are treated, an ECG review should be considered before treatment is started.
discuss with patients when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant or at their next review, the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours

items.t: Monitor for suicidality early and after dose changes; INR more often with oral anticoagulants; children: growth and puberty, mania.

src.q: patients should be closely monitored until such improvement occurs
Clinical monitoring, and more frequent monitoring of INR with oral anticoagulants, should be made.
Growth and pubertal development (height, weight, and TANNER staging) should therefore be monitored during and after treatment with fluoxetine.

items.t: Stop if: seizures (or more frequent), manic phase, unexplained rash/allergy, serotonin syndrome, signs of arrhythmia.

src.q: Treatment should be discontinued in any patient who develops seizures or where there is an increase in seizure frequency.
fluoxetine should be discontinued in any patient entering a manic phase

items.t: Single or divided dose, with or between meals.

src.q: Fluoxetine may be administered as a single or divided dose, during or between meals.

items.t: Do not drive or use machines until sure performance is not affected. Avoid alcohol.

src.q: Patients should be advised to avoid driving a car or operating hazardous machinery until they are reasonably certain that their performance is not affected.
the combination of SSRI treatment and alcohol is not advisable

items.t: Seek urgent help for new or worse suicidal thoughts (NHS 111, crisis team, Samaritans 116 123). Sexual problems may continue after stopping. Do not stop without advice.

src.q: You can call NHS 111, or your local mental health crisis team, Samaritans on 116 123
